title: Intel Stock (INTC) Falls 7.0% After Shareholder Lawsuit (Nov 16)
summary: Intel (INTC) fell 7.02% to $55.47 on Nov 16 as a shareholder class action and an AI chip selloff ahead of Nvidia's earnings weighed on the stock.
body_markdown:
## Why Intel Stock Fell


Financial media tied the drop first to a shareholder lawsuit. According to[Proactive](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/intel-shares-fall-6-shareholders-171000158.html) , citing Reuters, the City of Southfield Fire and Police Retirement System, a Michigan pension fund, filed a proposed class action on Friday in federal court in San Jose, California.


The suit covers investors who bought Intel shares between July 23 and October 29, 2026, names CEO Lip-Bu Tan and CFO David Zinsner as defendants, and alleges Intel did not promptly disclose how falling PC sales and an inventory buildup would hit revenue. The claims are unproven, and Intel had not immediately responded to a request for comment.


The complaint targets the run-up to Intel's nearly 29% one-day drop on October 30, as Proactive reported. According to Intel's[third-quarter 2026 results release](https://www.intc.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1786/intel-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results) on October 29, the company forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $15.0 billion to $16.0 billion, and CFO David Zinsner said, "we see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year."


The wider chip selloff added pressure. Per[24/7 Wall St.](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/intw-2x-intel-etf-tumbles-200312007.html) , AI-related chip stocks fell as Nvidia dragged the group lower ahead of its results. A[Motley Fool](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/why-intel-stock-falling-monday-183502050.html) writer argued that general market jitters were more to blame than the lawsuit, with[Nvidia's earnings report on Tuesday, November 17](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/nvidia-stock-earnings-preview-ceo-succession/) in focus.


## INTC Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Data Center and AI revenue rose 78% to $7.3 billion in the third quarter, and total revenue grew 21% to $16.5 billion, according to Intel's results release.
- In the same release, CEO Lip-Bu Tan said that "demand for our CPUs remains robust" despite near-term headwinds across the PC industry, a company view.
- Zinsner expects industry server CPU units to grow more than 30% in both 2026 and 2027, according to[TIKR](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/intel-trades-34x-pe-just-193934245.html) .


### Risks


- The Client Computing and Physical AI Group, Intel's largest segment, fell 5% to $8.1 billion in the third quarter, and management expects the PC slowdown to last at least through the first half of 2027.
- The class action seeks unspecified damages, per Proactive, and 24/7 Wall St. noted that its claims remain allegations.
- Intel has struggled to meet demand for data center server chips, which limits how much it can gain from AI infrastructure spending, Proactive reported.
- Intel Foundry lost $10.3 billion in 2025 on $17.8 billion of revenue, according to TIKR.
